test_title: PYST 12: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 24 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Which of the following statements are true regarding Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022?

1. The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 1 Dec 2022.

2. The Bill seeks to give effect to the Antarctic Treaty, the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources and the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty.

3. It also seeks to protect the Antarctic environment and regulate activities in the region.

4. The provisions of the Bill will apply to any person, vessel or aircraft that is a part of an Indian expedition to Antarctica under a permit issued under the Bill.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2, 3 and 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 **was introduced in **Lok Sabha on 1 April 2022**, not 1 December 2022.
 
• The Bill seeks to give effect to the Antarctic Treaty, the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources, and the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty.
 
• It also seeks to **protect the Antarctic environment **and regulate activities in the region.
 
• The provisions of the Bill will apply to any person, vessel, or aircraft that is a part of an Indian expedition to Antarctica under a permit issued under the Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Antarctic Treaty was **signed in 1959 and came into force in 1961**, with the aim to ensure that Antarctica is used for peaceful purposes and scientific research.
 
• India became a party to the Antarctic Treaty in 1983 and has since established research stations in the region, including** 'Maitri' and 'Bharati'**.
 
• The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 is the first domestic legislation aimed at regulating Indian activities in Antarctica, ensuring compliance with international agreements.
